item.research_question: Can a novel material descriptor based on valence shell electron distribution and local coordination effectively predict local magnetic moments, formation energies, and atomization energies while providing interpretability in terms of physical chemistry?
item.material_system: Bimetal alloys of lanthanide metal and transition-metal (LAT) including Mn, Fe, Co, Ni; LATX alloys (X = B, C, N, O); transition-metal binary alloys (TT); organic molecules from the QM7 dataset
item.processing_route: Computed local magnetic moments using VASP 5.4.1 with GGA/PBE functional, 520 eV energy cutoff, 150 k-point mesh density, and 0.1eV Gaussian smearing; constructed Orbital-Field Matrix (OFM) descriptors using Voronoi polyhedra for coordination numbers and inverse distance weighting; performed decision tree regression and Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR) with Laplacian kernel
item.test_conditions: Cross-validated on 658 LAT structures for magnetic moments; 4000+ crystalline compounds (LATX, TTX, LAT, TT) for formation energies; 6915 organic molecules (QM7) for atomization energies
key_findings: OFM achieved a cross-validated RMSE of 0.19 eV/atom and R² of 0.98 for formation energies of crystalline systems, outperforming the Coulomb Matrix (CM) descriptor (RMSE 0.47 eV/atom, R² 0.87).
For local magnetic moments in LAT alloys, KRR using OFM yielded an RMSE of 0.13 μB and R² of 0.93, slightly better than the CM descriptor (RMSE 0.15 μB, R² 0.90).
Decision tree analysis revealed that the magnetic moment of Fe sites is less than 2.0 μB when the coordination number of occupied d orbitals is less than 6.6 or greater than 9.15.
For Ni sites, a large magnetic moment (> 1.0 μB) is obtained when the coordination number of occupied d orbitals is greater than 8.25.
The OFM descriptor for the QM7 organic molecules dataset required only 25 non-zero features despite high dimensionality, whereas LATX datasets exhibited a large variety of OFMs.
The OFM achieved a cross-validated RMSE of 0.043 eV/atom and R² of 0.98 for atomization energies of organic molecules, comparable to the CM descriptor (RMSE 0.040 eV/atom, R² 0.99).
The OFM demonstrated superior prediction ability for LATX systems with high diversity in atomic composition and structure compared to the CM approach.
item.mechanism: The OFM encodes the coordination of valence electrons and the number of orbitals j coordinating the center orbital i, incorporating distance-dependent weights via inverse distance. This representation captures the ligand field and crystal field effects, where the coordination numbers of occupied d orbitals of transition-metals and occupied f orbitals of lanthanides determine local magnetic moments through T-T and LA-T exchange interactions.
item.limitations: The OFM includes the effect of nearest neighbor sites chosen by Voronoi polyhedra only, potentially missing long-range interactions that the CM descriptor captures via power-law decay; for simple organic molecules (QM7), the CM descriptor yields slightly better results than OFM.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that OFM could be useful for mining chemical/physical information on materials from available datasets using modern machine learning algorithms and for the theoretical design of materials properties via an approach similar to building blocks.
quotes: We propose a novel representation of materials named an 'orbital-field matrix (OFM)', which is based on the distribution of valence shell electrons.

The decision trees learned from the LAT alloy data show that the coordination numbers of the occupied d orbitals of the transition-metals and the occupied f orbitals of the lanthanides play important roles in determining the local magnetic moments of the transition-metal sites.

Our computational experiments show that the OFM representation can accurately reproduce the local magnetic moments of transition-metal sites in LAT alloys, formation energies of crystalline systems, and atomization energies of molecular systems.
